title: Bot trace record
description: One record per bot action. Genre-neutral: instantiate action, resources, goals and snapshot per game. A trace is an array of these.

t.description: Action index, or simulated time. Monotonic within a trace.

persona.description: Frozen per release. Screens are tuned to bots, never bots to screens.

seed.description: Same seed + same actions must reproduce the same state.

action.description: The action taken, in the game's own action vocabulary.

legal_action_count.description: Size of the legal action set at this state. Zero progress-making moves is a dead end.

result.description: Short summary of what the action did.

progress.description: Whether this action made progress. Runs of false are stalls; a state where no legal action can set this true is a dead end.

goals.description: Visible goals and whether each is completable now. Drives the anticipation fraction.

resources.description: Resource name to amount. Empty object is legal for games with no resources.

events.description: Big changes at this action. first_seen_item / first_reached_tier / system_unlocked are what make the novelty interval computable; an events list containing only rewards cannot measure novelty.

magnitude.description: Outcome size, for the escalation metric. Must be monotonic with the feedback the player receives.

decision.description: Optimizer-only. Feeds the decision index: always-large gap means one obvious move, always-near-zero means the choice does not matter.

distinct_from_second.description: True when the top two moves differ in kind, not just in value. Close AND different is what an interesting decision looks like.

snapshot.description: ASCII rendering of the state. Emitted every N actions and at every big change, so a reader can see the state without replaying.

foreseeable.description: Was the consequence visible in the state at the time. Expensive AND unforeseeable is the punishing case.

recovery_cost.description: Actions until prior progress was regained. Filled by the scorer.
